newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia's Air Baltic gets new SAS manager.
newsitem.headline: Latvia's Air Baltic gets new SAS manager.

text.p: Latvian airline Air Baltic, part-owned by Scandinavian Airlines, on Wednesday said a new company president had been appointed.
New president Rudi Schwab will join the company on March 20 and has worked for SAS for 25 years. Most recently, he managed SAS in Korea and Japan, Air Baltic said in a statement.
He replaces outgoing company chief Kjell Fredheim, who has led Air Baltic since it was created in 1995 from former state-owned airline Latavio. The government still owns 51 percent of Air Baltic.
Air Baltic said that in 1996 the company carried 115,000 passengers to around 11 countries.
It uses only Western aircraft, including Avros and Boeing jets.
